sam: Ran nsys + perfetto on a prod-like 8xA100 job for the 70B model (batch=16, seq=2048). NV capture shows the KV-cache write path is a top hotspot, taking ~40-50% of GPU time in the worst slices. Perfetto trace: https://perfetto/reports/1748120000 (private).

sam: nsys command I used:
```
nsys profile -o out.nsys --trace=nvtx,cuda,cudnn python -m runtime.bench --model redwood/70b --batch 16 --seq 2048 --workers 8
```

sam: Quick kernel timeline excerpt from perfetto (simplified):
```
[0] fused_attention_forward        12.3ms
[1] kv_cache_read                  1.1ms
[2] kv_cache_write                 8.9ms  <-- big tail contributor
[3] flash_attention_forward        3.1ms
[4] softmax                        0.7ms
[5] cudaMemcpyAsync (DtoD)         2.4ms  (stream 2 blocking)
```

jia: Interesting — do we see host <-> device copies interleaved or purely device-local?
sam: Perfetto shows Device-to-Device memcpy on stream 2 serializing right before fused_attn on stream 0. Not H2D, but the memcpy appears to synchronize some barriers (probably writing KV pages).

maria: Could be uncoalesced stores from the fused kernel writing out KV slots. If stores are strided we lose write coalescing and get long tail.

ryan: What's our runtime kernel selector policy currently?
sam: Selector currently: prefer fused when seq <= 512 and num_heads % 8 == 0, else flash. It's tuned on median latency; doesn't consider KV write footprint or tail percentiles.

jia: That explains mismatch — we have many requests at 1024-2048 at tail and selector still picks fused for some batches because of head divisibility. We should add workload-aware heuristics (tail-aware).

maria: Proposal: add a small runtime estimator measured over sliding window of requests that tracks kv_write_time and kv_write_bytes. If kv_write_time_p95 > X then favor flash variant for that route.

sam: Opened initial perf PR with raw traces and tables: https://git/repo/pull/4182 (contains nsys output and perfetto links).

devops-bot: Canary rollout queued for group "canary-attn" at 04:00 UTC :rocket:

jia: Quick local ablation results posted to the PR:
- batch16 seq2048 kv-cold: fused p99=180ms, flash p99=120ms
- batch16 seq2048 kv-warm: fused p99=95ms, flash p99=90ms

sam: Those numbers are telling — cold KV makes fused much worse. Warmed KV reduces the gap, so write cost / initial allocation looks like the culprit.

maria: I'll prototype changing KV layout (AoS -> SoA) to try to coalesce writes and also add a buffered write merge to reduce number of small stores. Filed issue #589 for that work.

ryan: Suggestion: in the selector, consider two cheap signals: sequence_length and a running kv_write_p95 metric. If seq > 1024 OR kv_write_p95 > 2ms then bias to flash. Jia, can you prototype selector change?

jia: On it. I'll add a sampling probe that collects a lightweight timestamp before/after kv write kernel and reports to the route stats. Then selector reads stats every 30s.

sam: Also noticed fused version issues with SM occupancy stalls when many small kernels are enqueued; batching heuristics may be fragmenting requests. We should try coalescing small concurrent requests into fused batch groups when memory allows.

maria: Another angle: memory alloc side-effects. Fused uses different temporary buffers causing extra cudaMallocs on cold paths. We should ensure allocator reuse paths are warm for both fused and flash.

jia: Running the change-set: selector sampling + probe + small canary. Will post perfetto traces once canary runs.

sam: Artifacts uploaded to s3: s3://redwood-inference/perf/1748120000/ (nsys.out, perfetto.pbz, csv latency tables).

ryan: Prioritization for sprint: 1) selector tail-aware tweak (jia) 2) KV layout + buffered write (maria) 3) allocator warmup + reduce malloc churn (sam) 4) run full 8x A100 perf sweep and compare.

devops-bot: Canary rollout started for "canary-attn" (4 hosts). Monitoring logs and perf traces.

jia: Initial canary micro-results: after selector biasing, observed 20-30% reduction in p99 on mixed seq workloads (not final). Will attach full trace when done.

maria: Pushed KV layout prototype branch. Initial microbenchmark shows 35% fewer global stores and 2x better store coalescing on synthetic pattern. Needs integration tests.

sam: Great work. Once maria's layout merges we'll re-run perfetto and nsys on canary and then decide global rollout. I'll update PR #4182 and the issue #589 with formatted traces.

ryan: Assigning tasks: jia -> selector patch & integration, maria -> KV layout+merge PR, sam -> perf artifact collection + canary ops. ETA end of week.

sam: Thanks all. Will keep thread updated with final perfetto timelines and kernel flame charts. :thumbsup:
